title: Arakhin 20
description: Rava’s chain of dilemmas about assessing a man twice ends, and a new mishna sets valuation against assessment: when heirs must pay, a limb on which life depends, “half my valuation” and “the valuation of half of me”, and then a bull pledged as a burnt offering that dies before it is brought.
topics: 🔁 Rava’s dilemmas: “my assessment” twice, “twice my assessment”, and a man assessed for no reason
⚰️ Valuation passes to the heirs, assessment does not: “there is no monetary value for the dead”
📜 Stringencies of vows over valuations: animals, birds and no allowance for means
✋ A forearm or a leg: “he has not said anything”, and Rav Giddel’s “he gives its assessment”
❤️ Head, liver, half of me and the leg above the knee: anything on which life depends
➗ “Half my valuation”: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda’s “flogged” and Rav Pappa’s decree
🛏️ At Rava’s sickbed: the Rabbis hold with Rabbi Meir and with Rabbi Shimon
🐂 “This bull is a burnt offering” or “upon me”: who bears the loss when it dies

a1.he: בְּחַד זִימְנָא אָמְדִינַן לֵיהּ, אוֹ דִלְמָא כֵּיוָן דִּבְזֶה אַחַר זֶה נָדַר, תְּרֵי זִימְנֵי אָמְדִינַן לֵיהּ?

a2.he: וְאִם תִּמְצָא לוֹמַר: כֵּיוָן דִּבְזֶה אַחַר זֶה נָדַר תְּרֵי זִימְנֵי אָמְדִינַן לֵיהּ, אָמַר: ״שְׁנֵי דָּמַי עָלַי״ בְּבַת אַחַת, מַהוּ? הָכָא וַדַּאי בְּבַת אַחַת נָדַר, בְּבַת אַחַת אָמְדִינַן לֵיהּ, אוֹ דִלְמָא כֵּיוָן דְּקָאָמַר ״שְׁנֵי״, כְּזֶה אַחַר זֶה דָּמֵי?

a3.he: אִם תִּימְצֵי לוֹמַר: כֵּיוָן דְּקָאָמַר ״שְׁנֵי״ כְּזֶה אַחַר זֶה דָּמֵי, אֲמָדוּהוּ מֵאֵלָיו מַהוּ? מִי אָמְרִינַן: הָא אֲמִיד מֵאֵלָיו וְקָאֵי, אוֹ דִלְמָא בָּעֵינַן כַּוָּונָה לְאוּמְדָּנָא?

a4.he: פְּשׁוֹט מִיהָא חֲדָא, דִּתְנַן: ״דְּמֵי עָלַי״ וּמֵת — לֹא יִתְּנוּ יוֹרְשִׁין, שֶׁאֵין דָּמִים לַמֵּתִים.

a5.he: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ אֲמָדוּהוּ מֵאֵלָיו הָוֵי אוּמְדָּנָא, הָא אֲמִיד וְקָאֵי, מִי אִיכָּא גַּבְרָא דְּלָא שָׁוֵי אַרְבְּעָה זוּזֵי?

a6.he: אֲמָדוּהוּ מֵאֵלָיו — נְחֵית לְאוּמְדָּנָא, ״דָּמַי עָלַי״ — לָא נְחֵית לְאוּמְדָּנָא.

a7.he: מַתְנִי׳ חוֹמֶר בָּעֲרָכִין מִבַּנְּדָרִים, כֵּיצַד? הָאוֹמֵר: ״עֶרְכִּי עָלַי״ וָמֵת — יִתְּנוּ הַיּוֹרְשִׁים, ״דָּמַי עָלַי״ וָמֵת — לֹא יִתְּנוּ הַיּוֹרְשִׁים, שֶׁאֵין דָּמִים לַמֵּתִים.

a8.he: ״עֵרֶךְ יָדִי״, וְ״עֵרֶךְ רַגְלִי עָלַי״ — לָא אָמַר כְּלוּם. ״עֵרֶךְ רֹאשִׁי״, וְ״עֵרֶךְ כְּבֵידִי עָלַי״ — נוֹתֵן עֵרֶךְ כּוּלּוֹ. זֶה הַכְּלָל: דָּבָר שֶׁהַנְּשָׁמָה תְּלוּיָה בּוֹ — נוֹתֵן עֵרֶךְ כּוּלּוֹ.

a9.he: ״חֲצִי עֶרְכִּי עָלַי״ — נוֹתֵן חֲצִי עֶרְכּוֹ, ״עֵרֶךְ חֶצְיִי עָלַי״ — נוֹתֵן עֵרֶךְ כּוּלּוֹ, ״חֲצִי דָּמַי עָלַי״ — נוֹתֵן חֲצִי דָּמָיו, ״דְּמֵי חֶצְיִי עָלַי״ — נוֹתֵן דְּמֵי כוּלּוֹ. זֶה הַכְּלָל: דָּבָר שֶׁהַנְּשָׁמָה תְּלוּיָה בּוֹ — נוֹתֵן דְּמֵי כוּלּוֹ.

a10.he: הָאוֹמֵר: ״עֶרְכּוֹ שֶׁל פְּלוֹנִי עָלַי״, מֵת הַנּוֹדֵר וְהַנִּידָּר — יִתְּנוּ הַיּוֹרְשִׁין. ״דָּמָיו שֶׁל פְּלוֹנִי עָלַי״, וּמֵת הַנּוֹדֵר — יִתְּנוּ הַיּוֹרְשִׁין, מֵת הַנִּידָּר — לֹא יִתְּנוּ הַיּוֹרְשִׁין, שֶׁאֵין דָּמִים לַמֵּתִים.

a11.he: גְּמָ׳ תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: חוֹמֶר בַּנְּדָרִים מִבַּעֲרָכִין, שֶׁהַנְּדָרִים חָלִין עַל בְּהֵמָה חַיָּה וָעוֹף, וְאֵין נִדּוֹנִים בְּהֶשֵּׂג יָד, מָה שֶׁאֵין כֵּן בָּעֲרָכִין.

a12.he: חוֹמֶר בָּעֲרָכִין מִבַּנְּדָרִים, כֵּיצַד? אָמַר: ״עֶרְכִּי עָלַי״ וָמֵת — יִתְּנוּ יוֹרְשִׁין, ״דָּמַי עָלַי״ וָמֵת — לֹא יִתְּנוּ יוֹרְשִׁין, שֶׁאֵין דָּמִים לַמֵּתִים.

a13.he: אָמַר ״עֶרְכִּי עָלַי״ וָמֵת — יִתְּנוּ יוֹרְשִׁין. שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ מִלְוָה עַל פֶּה גּוֹבֶה מִן הַיּוֹרְשִׁין? שָׁאנֵי הָכָא, דְּמִלְוָה כְּתוּבָה בַּתּוֹרָה הִיא.

a14.he: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: מִלְוָה הַכְּתוּבָה בַּתּוֹרָה כִּכְתוּבָה בִּשְׁטָר דָּמְיָא? הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן — כְּשֶׁעָמַד בַּדִּין.

a15.he: דִּכְוָותַהּ גַּבֵּי ״דָּמַי עָלַי״ שֶׁעָמַד בַּדִּין, אַמַּאי לֹא יִתְּנוּ יוֹרְשִׁין ״דָּמַי עָלַי״? מְחוּסַּר אוּמְדָּנָא. ״עֶרְכִּי עָלַי״ — לֹא מְחוּסָּר וְלֹא כְלוּם.

a16.he: עֵרֶךְ יָדִי וְרַגְלִי עָלַי וְכוּ׳. אָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב: וְנוֹתֵן דָּמֶיהָ.

a17.he: וְהָא ״לֹא אָמַר כְּלוּם״ קָתָנֵי! לֹא אָמַר כְּלוּם לְרַבָּנַן, וְנוֹתֵן דָּמֶיהָ לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר.

a18.he: הָא אַמְרַהּ חֲדָא זִימְנָא, דְּאָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב: הָאוֹמֵר ״עֵרֶךְ כְּלִי זֶה עָלַי״ נוֹתֵן דָּמָיו!

a19.he: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: הָתָם הוּא דְּאָדָם יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁאֵין עֵרֶךְ לִכְלִי, וְגָמַר וְאָמַר לְשֵׁם דָּמִים, אֲבָל הָכָא מִיטְעָא קָטָעֵי, דְּסָבַר כִּי הֵיכִי דְּאִיכָּא ״עֵרֶךְ רֹאשִׁי״ וְ״עֵרֶךְ כְּבֵידִי״, אִיכָּא נָמֵי ״עֵרֶךְ יָדִי״ וְ״עֵרֶךְ רַגְלִי״, אֲבָל דְּמֵי לָא קָאָמַר — קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

a20.he: ״עֵרֶךְ רֹאשִׁי״ וְ״עֵרֶךְ כְּבֵידִי״ — נוֹתֵן עֵרֶךְ כּוּלּוֹ. מַאי טַעְמָא? ״נְפָשׁוֹת״ קָאָמַר רַחֲמָנָא.

a21.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל: דָּבָר שֶׁהַנְּשָׁמָה תְּלוּיָה בּוֹ וכו׳. לְאֵתוֹיֵי מִן הָאַרְכּוּבָּה וּלְמַעְלָה.

a22.he: חֲצִי עֶרְכִּי עָלַי נוֹתֵן כּוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״חֲצִי עֶרְכִּי עָלַי״ — נוֹתֵן חֲצִי עֶרְכּוֹ. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: לוֹקֶה וְנוֹתֵן עֵרֶךְ שָׁלֵם.

a23.he: לוֹקֶה?! אַמַּאי? אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לוֹקֶה בְּעֵרֶךְ שָׁלֵם, מַאי טַעְמָא? גְּזֵירָה ״חֲצִי (עֶרְכִּי) [עֶרְכּוֹ]״ אַטּוּ ״עֵרֶךְ חֶצְיוֹ״, וְעֵרֶךְ חֶצְיוֹ הָוֵי דָּבָר שֶׁהַנְּשָׁמָה תְּלוּיָה בּוֹ.

a24.he: ״חֲצִי דָּמַי עָלַי״ — נוֹתֵן כּוּ׳. ״דְּמֵי חֶצְיִי עָלַי״ — נוֹתֵן דְּמֵי כּוּלּוֹ, מַאי טַעְמָא?

a26.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל: דָּבָר שֶׁהַנְּשָׁמָה תְּלוּיָה בּוֹ, לְאֵתוֹיֵי מִן הָאַרְכּוּבָּה וּלְמַעְלָה.

a27.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַמַּעֲרִיךְ חֲצִי עֵרֶךְ כְּלִי, רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: נוֹתֵן דָּמָיו, וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: לֹא אָמַר כְּלוּם. רָבָא חֲלַשׁ, עוּל לְגַבֵּיהּ אַבָּיֵי וְרַבָּנַן, וְיָתְבִי וְקָאָמְרִי: בִּשְׁלָמָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר קָסָבַר אֵין אָדָם מוֹצִיא דְּבָרָיו לְבַטָּלָה, לָא שְׁנָא כּוּלּוֹ וְלָא שְׁנָא חֶצְיוֹ.

a28.he: אֶלָּא רַבָּנַן מַאי קָסָבְרִי? אִי אָדָם מוֹצִיא דְּבָרָיו לְבַטָּלָה — אֲפִילּוּ כּוּלּוֹ נָמֵי, וְאִי אֵין אָדָם מוֹצִיא דְּבָרָיו לְבַטָּלָה — אֲפִילּוּ חֶצְיוֹ נָמֵי!

a29.he: אֲמַר לְהוּ רָבָא וְאַבָּיֵי: רַבָּנַן דְּהָכָא כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר סָבְרִי לַהּ, וְסָבְרִי לַהּ כְּרַבִּי׳ שִׁמְעוֹן. סָבְרִי לַהּ כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר, דְּאָמַר: ״אֵין אָדָם מוֹצִיא דְּבָרָיו לְבַטָּלָה״.

a30.he: וְסָבְרִי לַהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, דְּאָמַר שֶׁלֹּא הִתְנַדֵּב כְּדֶרֶךְ הַמִּתְנַדְּבִים; כּוּלֵּיהּ אוֹרְחֵיהּ לְאִיתְנַדּוֹבֵי, פַּלְגֵיהּ לָאו אוֹרְחֵיהּ לְאִיתְנַדּוֹבֵי.

a31.he: הָאוֹמֵר ״עֶרְכּוֹ שֶׁל פְּלוֹנִי עָלַי״, וּמֵת הַנּוֹדֵר כּוּ׳. מַאי נִיהוּ? שֶׁעָמַד בַּדִּין.

a32.he: הַיְינוּ הָךְ! סֵיפָא אִיצְטְרִיךְ לֵיהּ, דָּמָיו שֶׁל פְּלוֹנִי עָלָיו, וּמֵת הַנּוֹדֵר — יִתְּנוּ הַיּוֹרְשִׁים.

b1.he: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא, כֵּיוָן דְּלָא אֲמָדוּהוּ לָא אִישְׁתַּעְבּוּד נִכְסֵי, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן: כֵּיוָן דְּעָמַד בַּדִּין אִישְׁתַּעְבּוֹדֵי אִישְׁתַּעְבּוּד נִכְסֵי, וְאוּמְדָּנָא גַּלּוֹיֵי מִילְּתָא בְעָלְמָא הוּא.

b2.he: מַתְנִי׳ ״שׁוֹר זֶה עוֹלָה״, וּ״בַיִת זֶה קׇרְבָּן״, וּמֵת הַשּׁוֹר וְנָפַל הַבַּיִת — פָּטוּר מִלְּשַׁלֵּם. ״שׁוֹר זֶה עָלַי עוֹלָה״, וּ״בַיִת זֶה עָלַי קׇרְבָּן״, מֵת הַשּׁוֹר וְנָפַל הַבַּיִת — חַיָּיב לְשַׁלֵּם.

b3.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר רַב: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא דְּאָמַר ״דְּמֵי שׁוֹר זֶה עָלַי עוֹלָה״, אֲבָל אָמַר ״שׁוֹר זֶה עָלַי עוֹלָה״, כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר ״זֶה״ וָמֵת — אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב בְּאַחְרָיוּתוֹ, ״עָלַי לַהֲבִיאוֹ״ קָאָמַר.

b4.he: מֵיתִיבִי: שׁוֹר זֶה עוֹלָה — הַשּׁוֹר הֶקְדֵּשׁ וּמוֹעֲלִין בּוֹ, מֵת אוֹ נִגְנַב — אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב בְּאַחְרָיוּתוֹ. ״שׁוֹר זֶה עָלַי עוֹלָה״ — הַשּׁוֹר הֶקְדֵּשׁ וּמוֹעֲלִין בּוֹ, מֵת אוֹ נִגְנַב — חַיָּיב בְּאַחְרָיוּתוֹ.

b5.he: מִי אַלִּימָא מִמַּתְנִיתִין, דְּאוֹקֵימְנָא דְּקָאָמַר ״דְּמֵי״? הָכָא נָמֵי דְּקָאָמַר ״דְּמֵי״.

b6.he: וְהָא מִדְּסֵיפָא דְּקָאָמַר ״דְּמֵי״, רֵישָׁא דְּלָא קָאָמַר ״דְּמֵי״! דְּקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא: דְּמֵי שׁוֹר עוֹלָה — הַשּׁוֹר חוּלִּין וְאֵין מוֹעֲלִין בּוֹ, מֵת אוֹ נִגְנַב — אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב בְּאַחְרָיוּתוֹ, אָבֵל חַיָּיב בְּאַחְרָיוּת דָּמָיו!

b7.he: רֵישָׁא וְסֵיפָא דְּקָאָמַר ״דְּמֵי״, רֵישָׁא דְּאָמַר: ״יִקְדַּישׁ הַשּׁוֹר לְדָמָיו״, וְסֵיפָא דְּקָאָמַר: ״לִכְשֶׁיָּבֹאוּ דָּמָיו יִקְדְּשׁוּ״.

b8.he: וְהָא אֵין אָדָם מַקְדִּישׁ דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא בָּא לָעוֹלָם? אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: הָא מַנִּי? רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא, דְּאָמַר: אָדָם מַקְדִּישׁ דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא בָּא לָעוֹלָם.

b9.he: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא לְרַב חִסְדָּא: כְּמַאן? כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר, דְּאָמַר: אָדָם מַקְדִּישׁ דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא בָּא לָעוֹלָם? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְאֶלָּא כְּמַאן?

b10.he: וְאִיכָּא דְּמַתְנֵי לַהּ אַהָא, הַמַּשְׂכִּיר בַּיִת לַחֲבֵרוֹ וְנִתְנַגֵּעַ, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחֲלָטוֹ כֹּהֵן, אוֹמֵר לוֹ: ״הֲרֵי שֶׁלְּךָ לְפָנֶיךָ״, נְתָצוֹ — חַיָּיב לְהַעֲמִיד לוֹ בַּיִת.

messages.text: Continued from 19b: Rava’s chain of dilemmas about vows of assessment. His last case so far: one said “My assessment is incumbent upon me”, and before the court assessed him he said it again. Do we say that here certainly…
we assess him once and he donates twice the value of that single assessment, or perhaps since he vowed sequentially we assess him twice?

notes.he: פי שנים בדמים יתן:
notes.en: We assess him once: and he gives twice the amount.

messages.text: And if you say in that case that since he vowed sequentially we assess him twice, if he says at the same time: My assessment is twice incumbent upon me, what is the halakha?

Do we say that here certainly he vowed at the same time, and therefore we assess him once, or perhaps since he says the word: Twice, it is considered as though he vowed sequentially and therefore he must be assessed twice?

Finally, if you say that since he says the word: Twice, it is considered as though he vowed sequentially and he must be assessed twice, if a court of ten assessed him on its own, i.e., not for the purpose of assessing a vow, what is the halakha?

notes.he: בלא שום צורך אלא לשום דברים בעלמא ועשרה היו שם מהו:
notes.en: They assessed him on his own: without any need, just in passing as talk, and ten were present; what is the halakha?

notes.dh: אמדוהו מאליו מהו מי אמרי' כו'
notes.he: הא בעיא לא אתיא בואם תמצא לומר כמו ההיא דלעיל ולבדה היה יכול לשאלה אלא שרוצה לערבה עם שאר הבעיות:
notes.en: They assessed him on his own, what is the halakha? Do we say etc.: this dilemma does not follow with “if you say” from the one before it, like the earlier ones; he could have asked it on its own, but he wanted to combine it with the other dilemmas.

notes.he: אמדוהו מאליו שלא אמר דמי עלי:
notes.en: They assessed him on his own: when he had not said, “My assessment is incumbent upon me.”

messages.text: Do we say that he has already been assessed on his own and now stands before us, and therefore there is no need for another assessment, or perhaps we require an assessment to be performed with intent for the sake of consecration to the Temple treasury.

Resolve at least one of these dilemmas, as we learned in the mishna below: In the case of one who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate my assessment, and then dies, his heirs need not give his assessment to the Temple treasury, as there is no monetary value for the dead, and his assessment at the time of his vow is unknown.

notes.he: מתני' חדא מהני בעיות:
notes.en: Resolve from this: [from] our mishna, one of these dilemmas.

notes.he: ומעיקרא לא ידעינן כמה שוה:
notes.en: As there is no monetary value for the dead: and from the outset we do not know how much he was worth.

notes.he: שאין אדם יכול לידע מאחר שמת כמה הוא שוה כשהוא חי:
notes.en: As there is no monetary value for the dead: for once he has died, a person cannot know how much he was worth when he was alive.

messages.text: And if it enters your mind that in a case where a court of ten assessed him on its own it is a valid assessment with regard to his vow, why does the mishna state that his heirs do not have to donate to the Temple treasury? Isn’t he considered as standing assessed from the outset, as is there a person who is not worth at least four zuz? This proves that an assessment is required to be performed with intent for the sake of consecration to the Temple treasury.

notes.he: דהא אין לך אדם שאינו שוה ד' זוזי:
notes.en: Isn’t he standing assessed: for there is no person who is not worth four zuz.

notes.he: מי איכא גברא דלא שוה ד' זוזי כשהוא חי והוה כי אמיד וליתבו יורשין (לא) דמי:
notes.en: Is there a man who is not worth four zuz while alive? So it is as though he had been assessed, and the heirs should give [his] assessment.

messages.text: The Gemara rejects this resolution: In a case where a court of ten assessed him on its own before he took his vow, he has entered into an assessment, i.e., an assessment has actually been performed. By contrast, in the case of one who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate my assessment, and then dies, he has not entered into an assessment, i.e., no actual assessment has been conducted at all.

notes.he: שלא נאמד מעולם אלא השתא הוא דאמדינן ואנן אומדנא בעינן:
notes.en: He has not entered into an assessment: he was never assessed; only now would we assess him, and we require an assessment.

notes.he: ודקדקו בו כמה היה שוה:
notes.en: When they assessed him on his own, he entered into an assessment: and they examined carefully how much he was worth.

notes.he: ומת לא נחית מעיקרא לאומדנא גמורה הלכך לא יתנו היורשין:
notes.en: “My assessment is incumbent upon me,” and he died: he never entered into a complete assessment in the first place; therefore the heirs do not give.

messages.text: Mishna

There are halakhot that are more stringent with regard to valuations than with regard to vows of assessment. How so? In the case of one who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate my valuation, and then dies, his heirs must give his valuation to the Temple treasury.

notes.he: דבר קצוב הוא הלכך יתנו היורשין:
notes.en: Mishna. My valuation is incumbent upon me: it is a fixed sum, so the heirs give it.

messages.text: But one who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate my assessment, and then dies, his heirs need not give his assessment to the Temple treasury, as there is no monetary value for the dead.

notes.he: והא דתניא בב"ק (דף כז.) ונתן פדיון נפשו דמי ניזק התם הוא טעמא משום דמשעתא דאזיק רמי עליה לשלומי כשעת ההיזק וההיא שעתא דאזקיה חי הוא אבל דמי עלי שאינו נודר אלא מה שישומוהו ב"ד והרי לא בא לידי כך שהרי מת לא יתנו היורשין:
notes.en: As there is no monetary value for the dead: and as for what is taught in Bava Kamma (27a) [about an ox that killed], “Then he shall give the ransom of his life” — the value of the one damaged — there the reason is that from the moment it did the damage, payment fell upon him as of the time of the damage, and at the time it damaged him he was alive. But with “My assessment is incumbent upon me,” he vows only what the court will assess him at, and he never came to that, since he died; [so] the heirs do not give.

notes.dh: דמי עלי ומת לא יתנו יורשים לפי שאין דמים וכו'
notes.he: והא דתניא בב"ק (דף כז. ושם) ונתן פדיון נפשו דמי ניזק פי' ששמין אותו לאחר מיתה כמה היה שוה מחיים גזירת הכתוב היא אבל הכא אינו נודר אלא דמים שישומוהו בב"ד והוא לא בא לידי שומא שהרי הוא מת לא יתנו יורשין את דמיו:
notes.en: “My assessment is incumbent upon me,” and he died, the heirs do not give, as there is no monetary value [for the dead] etc.: and as for what is taught in Bava Kamma (27a), “Then he shall give the ransom of his life,” the value of the one damaged, meaning that they assess him after his death at what he was worth while alive: that is a decree of Scripture. But here he vows only the value the court will assess him at, and he never came to an assessment, since he died; [so] the heirs do not give his value.

messages.text: One who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate the valuation of my forearm, or: The valuation of my leg, has not said anything, as there are valuations in the Torah only for a complete person.

But if one says: It is incumbent upon me to donate the valuation of my head, or: The valuation of my liver, he gives the valuation of his entire self. This is the principle: One who valuates an item upon which the soul is dependent, i.e., without which one will die, gives the valuation of his entire self.

notes.he: בערכך נפשות כתיב:
notes.en: He gives the valuation of his entire self: “a valuation of living people [nefashot]” is written.

messages.text: One who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate half of my valuation, gives half of his valuation. But one who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate the valuation of half of me, gives the valuation of his entire self.

notes.he: הוי כערך ראשי וערך כבידי דהוי דבר שהנשמה תלויה בו:
notes.en: The valuation of half of me is incumbent upon me: this is like “the valuation of my head” and “the valuation of my liver,” since it is something on which life depends.

messages.text: Likewise, one who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate half of my assessment, gives half of his assessment; one who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate the assessment of half of me, gives the assessment of his entire self. This is the principle: One who takes a vow with regard to an item upon which the soul is dependent gives the assessment of his entire self.

notes.dh: דמי חציי עלי נותן דמי כולו
notes.he: דהא תניא בפרק השג יד (לעיל ערכין יח.) הקשתה דמים לערכין לידון בכבודו:
notes.en: The assessment of half of me is incumbent upon me, he gives the assessment of his entire self: for it is taught in the chapter Hassag Yad (above, Arakhin 18a): you have juxtaposed assessments to valuations, to judge [a limb] by its importance.

messages.text: With regard to one who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate the valuation of so-and-so, and both the one who vowed and the object of the vow die, the heirs of the one who vowed must give the valuation of the object of the vow to the Temple treasury.

With regard to one who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate the assessment of so-and-so, and the one who vowed dies, his heirs must give his assessment to the Temple treasury. If the object of the vow dies, the heirs of the one who vowed need not give his assessment to the Temple treasury, as there is no monetary value for the dead.
Gemara

There are halakhot that are more stringent with regard to vows of assessment than with regard to valuations, as vows of assessment take effect with regard to a domesticated animal, an undomesticated animal, and a bird. If one says: It is incumbent upon me to donate the assessment of this bird, he must donate that assessment. This is not the case with regard to valuations, as they do not take effect with regard to animals and birds.

notes.he: אם אמר דמי בהמתי עלי אבל ערך אינו אלא באדם:
notes.en: Gemara. On a domesticated animal: if he said, “The assessment of my animal is incumbent upon me.” But a valuation applies only to a person.

notes.he: תימה אמאי לא פריך אמתני' דקתני זה חומר בנדרים מבערכין זה חומר ותו לא והא איכא הני דברייתא דכה"ג פריך בב"מ פרק הזהב (בבא מציעא דף נז:) גבי הא דאמר זה חומר בהקדש מבהדיוט ופריך זה חומר ותו לא האיכא טובא לפרוך הכא הכי וי"ל דהתם ליכא חידוש למצוא חומרא בהקדש מבהדיוט דמדין הוא דיש לנו להחמיר טפי בהקדש מבהדיוט ומש"ה קא מתמה עליה הש"ס זה חומר ותו לא והא איכא טובא אבל הכא דאיכא רבותא דמחמיר טפי בנדרים מבערכין מש"ה לא שייך למיפרך עליה זה חומר ותו לא דתנא ושייר:
notes.en: The Sages taught: more stringent with regard to vows than with regard to valuations etc.: it is puzzling: why does the Gemara not object to our mishna, which teaches “this is a stringency of vows over valuations” [so Tosafot; our mishna opens with the stringency of valuations over vows]: this stringency, and no more? But there are these of the baraita! The Gemara asks that way in Bava Metzia, chapter HaZahav (57b), about “this is a stringency of consecrated property over ordinary property,” objecting: “this stringency, and no more? There are many!” Let us ask the same here. One can answer that there, finding a stringency of consecrated property over ordinary property is no novelty, since it is only logical to be stricter with consecrated property than with ordinary property; that is why the Talmud wonders, “this stringency and no more? There are many.” But here, where it is a novelty to be stricter with vows than with valuations, it is not fitting to object, “this stringency and no more?”, since the tanna taught some and left some out.

messages.text: And another halakha that is more stringent with regard to vows of assessment than with regard to valuations is that the destitute who take vows of assessment are not assessed based on affordability. This is not the case with regard to valuations, which are assessed based on whether the one who vows can afford to pay what they vowed.

notes.he: שאם אמר דמי עלי ואין ידו משגת יתן הכל לכשיוכל:
notes.en: And they are not judged by affordability: if he said, “My assessment is incumbent upon me,” and he cannot afford it, he gives all of it when he is able.

notes.he: וקשה שהרי הקשנו לעיל (ערכין ד' יח.) דמים לערכין מרגלית לקלים ואין היקש למחצה ואיכא למימר דאיכא חד מיעוטא דכתיב יעריכנו הכהן גבי ערכין דמשמע ליה ולא לאחר וגבי ערכין נידון בהשג יד כאשר יעריכנו הכהן ולא גבי נדרים:
notes.en: And they are not judged by affordability, as valuations are: this is difficult, for above (Arakhin 18a) we juxtaposed assessments to valuations, [as in] “a pearl for the poor,” and there is no juxtaposition by halves [that is, a juxtaposition should apply in every respect]. One can say there is a single exclusion: regarding valuations it is written “the priest shall valuate him [ya’arikhenu],” which implies him and not another; so with valuations one is judged by affordability, “as the priest shall valuate him,” and not with vows.

notes.he: אלא נותן כל מה שיש לו וחוזר ונותן כשיהא לו:
notes.en: And is not judged by affordability: rather he gives all that he has, and gives again when he has more.

messages.text: There is a halakha that is more stringent with regard to valuations than with regard to vows of assessment. How so? In the case of one who said: It is incumbent upon me to donate my valuation, and dies, his heirs must give his valuation to the Temple treasury. But one who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate my assessment, and dies, his heirs need not give his assessment to the Temple treasury, as there is no monetary value for the dead.
The Gemara suggests one can conclude from this ruling that one collects a loan by oral agreement from the heirs, as no promissory note was written with regard to this obligation.
messages.quote: said: It is incumbent upon me to donate my valuation, and dies, his heirs must give

notes.he: ופלוגתא היא בכמה דוכתי:
notes.en: Conclude from this that a loan by oral agreement etc.: and this is a dispute in several places.

messages.text: The Gemara rejects this conclusion: Here the heirs’ obligation to pay the valuation of the deceased is different, i.e., it is not the same as a loan by oral agreement, as a valuation is considered a loan, i.e., debt, written in the Torah, in accordance with the deceased’s age and sex at the time of the vow.

notes.dh: שאני הכא דמלוה הכתובה בתורה היא
notes.he: דכיון שאמר ערכי עלי כבר כתוב בתורה כמה צריך ליתן:
notes.en: Here it is different, as it is a loan written in the Torah: since he said “My valuation is incumbent upon me,” it is already written in the Torah how much he must give.

messages.text: If so, can one conclude from the baraita that a loan that is written in the Torah, i.e., any financial obligation that applies by Torah law, is considered as though it were written in a document?

notes.he: ופלוגתא היא במס' בכורות בפ' יש בכור לנחלה (דף מט:):
notes.en: Conclude from this that a loan written [in the Torah] etc.: and this is a dispute in tractate Bekhorot, in the chapter Yesh Bekhor LaNaḥala (49b).

messages.text: The Gemara rejects this conclusion: Here we are dealing with a case where he stood in judgment before he died, and the court obligated him to donate his valuation. The court’s ruling is considered like a financial obligation written in a document, and therefore the heirs are required to pay his valuation.

notes.he: וחייבוהו קודם מותו דה"ל כמלוה בשטר:
notes.en: Where he stood in judgment: and they obligated him before his death, so that it is like a loan with a document.

notes.he: וחייבוהו ליתן וכל העומד לגבות כגבוי דמי:
notes.en: Where he stood in judgment: and they obligated him to give; and whatever stands to be collected is considered as collected.

messages.text: If so, then in the corresponding situation, with regard to one who said: It is incumbent upon me to donate my assessment, the baraita must also be referring to one who stood in judgment. But in that case, why don’t the heirs have to donate his assessment?

notes.he: הרי אמדוהו ב"ד:
notes.en: Why should the heirs not give: after all, the court has assessed him.

messages.text: In the case of one who said: It is incumbent upon me to donate my assessment, even if he stood in judgment and the court obligated him to pay, the assessment of the precise amount he must pay is still lacking, as that amount is determined only through the assessment of a court. By contrast, with regard to one who said: It is incumbent upon me to donate my valuation, if he stood in judgment and the court obligated him to pay, nothing is lacking, as the amount he pays is fixed by the Torah.

notes.he: שחייבוהו לשלם ולא הספיקו לאומדו עד שמת:
notes.en: It lacks an assessment: they obligated him to pay but did not manage to assess him before he died.

notes.he: בשעמד בדין ולא אמדוהו ומת ולא אמר כלום:
notes.en: It lacks an assessment: where he stood in judgment and they did not assess him, and he died. [The text runs on: “He has not said anything.”]

messages.text: And although he is exempt from donating the valuation, he must give the assessment of the forearm or leg.
messages.quote: It is incumbent upon me to donate the valuation of my forearm, or: The valuation of my leg

notes.he: דאין הנשמה תלויה בו:
notes.en: [A note in the printed text: it seems something is missing here, and it should read:] “The valuation of my hand and the valuation of my foot is incumbent upon me”: he has not said anything, since life does not depend on it. And he gives its assessment: of the hand, that is, etc., since life does not depend on it.

messages.text: But isn’t it taught in the mishna that he has not said anything?

The ruling of the mishna that he has not said anything applies according to the opinion of the Rabbis, but he must give the assessment according to the opinion of Rabbi Meir. Rabbi Meir maintains that a person does not utter a statement for naught, and therefore he must have intended to vow to donate the assessment of the limb, as there is no valuation for limbs.

notes.he: דאמרי בפ"ק (לעיל ערכין ה.) אדם מוציא דבריו לבטלה:
notes.en: He has not said anything, according to the Rabbis: who say in the first chapter (above, Arakhin 5a) that a person utters words for naught.

notes.he: ואוקימנא בפ"ק דאליבא דר"מ אמרה:
notes.en: He gives its assessment: and we established in the first chapter that he said it according to Rabbi Meir.

notes.he: של יד כלומר דאין אדם מוציא דבריו לבטלה וידוע שאין ערך ליד וגמר ואמר לשום דמים ונותן דמיה:
notes.en: And he gives its assessment: of the hand. That is, since a person does not utter his words for naught, and it is known that there is no valuation for a hand, he made up his mind and spoke for the sake of assessment, and he gives its assessment.

notes.he: לר"מ דאמר בפירקין קמא המעריך פחות מבן חודש ר"מ אומר נותן דמיו כו':
notes.en: According to Rabbi Meir, who says in our first chapter: one who valuates [an infant] less than a month old, Rabbi Meir says he gives its assessment, etc.

messages.text: But didn’t Rav Giddel already say it once?

In the case of one who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate the valuation of this vessel, although he is exempt from donating the valuation of the vessel, according to the opinion of Rabbi Meir he must give the assessment of the vessel.

It was necessary for Rav Giddel to repeat that halakha with regard to one who vowed the valuation of his forearm or leg, lest you say this ruling is applicable only there, with regard to a vessel, as a person knows that there is no valuation for a vessel, and he therefore intended and said his vow for the sake of assessments.

But here, with regard to his forearm or leg, he erred, as he thought that just as there is an obligation to donate the valuation in a case where one said: It is incumbent upon me to donate the valuation of my head, or: The valuation of my liver, so too, there is an obligation to donate the valuation if one said: It is incumbent upon me to donate the valuation of my forearm or the valuation of my leg. But he did not intend to say a vow of assessments.

notes.he: והלכך לא ליתיב דמי קמ"ל:
notes.en: But he did not say “assessment”: and therefore he should not give an assessment. [Rav Giddel] teaches us [that he does].

notes.dh: מיטעא קא טעי דסבר כו'] אבל דמי לא
notes.he: כלומר לשום דמים לא מתכוין ולא ליתן דמיה קמ"ל:
notes.en: He was mistaken, thinking etc.; but not “assessment”: that is, he did not intend it for the sake of assessment, and should not give its assessment. [Rav Giddel] teaches us [that he does].

messages.text: Therefore, Rav Giddel teaches us that even in the case of one who vowed to donate the valuation of his forearm or leg, he did not speak in error but intended to donate the assessment.

§ What is the reason? The Merciful One states: “A valuation of living people” (Leviticus 27:2), which indicates that in the case of one who valuates an item upon which the soul is dependent and without which one will die, he must give the valuation of his entire self.
messages.quote: the valuation of my head, or: The valuation of my liver, he gives the valuation of his entire self

verse.he: דַּבֵּר אֶל־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאָמַרְתָּ אֲלֵהֶם אִישׁ כִּי יַפְלִא נֶדֶר בְּעֶרְכְּךָ נְפָשֹׁת לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: Speak to the Israelite people and say to them: When anyone explicitly vows to GOD the equivalent for a human being,

messages.text: The phrase: This is the principle, serves to include one who vowed to donate the valuation of his leg from the knee and above. Since one would die if his leg were severed above the knee, this is considered an item upon which the soul is dependent, and therefore he gives the valuation of his entire self.
messages.quote: This is the principle: One who valuates an item upon which the soul is dependent

notes.he: שאם אמר ערך רגלי עלי מן הארכובה ולמעלה נותן ערך כולו:
notes.en: To include from the knee and above: if he said, “The valuation of my leg, from the knee and above, is incumbent upon me,” he gives the valuation of his entire self.

messages.text: One who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate half of my valuation, gives half of his valuation.
messages.quote: It is incumbent upon me to donate half of my valuation, gives half of his valuation

messages.text: He is flogged and must give his full valuation.
Since he did not commit a sin, why is he flogged?

He is flogged, i.e., punished, in that he must donate his full valuation. What is the reason he needs to give his full valuation? A rabbinic decree was issued that one who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate half of my valuation, must give the value of his entire self, due to a concern that this case might become confused with the similar one of a person who vows to donate the valuation of half of himself.
And the halakha in such a case is that he must give the value of his entire self, as the valuation of half of him is an item upon which the soul is dependent.

The mishna further teaches that one who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate half of my assessment, gives half of his assessment. But one who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate the assessment of half of me, gives the assessment of his entire self, as one who takes a vow of assessment with regard to an item upon which the soul depends must give the assessment of his entire self.

What is the reason? After all, it is only with regard to valuations that the Torah states: “A valuation of living people” (Leviticus 27:2), indicating that one who valuates an item upon which the soul depends must give the valuation of his entire self; but this is not stated with regard to assessments.

It is written: “When a man shall clearly utter a vow [neder] with regard to a valuation [be’erkekha] of living people” (Leviticus 27:2). The verse juxtaposes vows of assessment [neder] and valuations [erekh], thereby teaching that just as one who takes a vow of valuation with regard to an item upon which the soul depends must give the valuation of his entire self, so too, one who takes a vow of assessment with regard to an item upon which the soul is dependent must give the assessment of his entire self.

verse.he: דַּבֵּר אֶל־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאָמַרְתָּ אֲלֵהֶם אִישׁ כִּי יַפְלִא נֶדֶר בְּעֶרְכְּךָ נְפָשֹׁת לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: Speak to the Israelite people and say to them: When anyone explicitly vows to GOD the equivalent for a human being,

notes.he: הוקשו נדרים לערכין:
notes.en: A vow by your valuation: vows were juxtaposed to valuations.

notes.he: [מ"ט נדר בערכך כתיב כלומר כל שישנו בערכין ישנו בדמים דהיינו נדר]:
notes.en: [What is the reason? “A vow by your valuation” is written; that is, whatever applies to valuations applies to assessments, which is “a vow.”]

messages.text: The phrase: This is the principle, serves to include one who vowed to donate the assessment of his leg from the knee and above. Since one would die if his leg were severed above the knee, this is an item upon which the soul depends, and therefore he gives the assessment of his entire self.
messages.quote: This is the principle: One who takes a vow with regard to an item upon which the soul is dependent

notes.he: וא"ת אמאי נקט מן הארכובה ולמעלה טפי מכל שאר י"ח טריפות וי"ל דאיכא רבותא בהאי טפי לאפוקי דר"ש דאמר (חולין דף מב:) יכולה היא ליכוות ולחיות:
notes.en: To include from the knee and above: and if you ask, why does he mention the leg from the knee and above rather than any of the other eighteen tereifot [injuries from which an animal cannot survive]? One can say that this one is more of a novelty, to exclude the view of Rabbi Shimon, who says (Ḥullin 42b) that it can be cauterized and live.

messages.caption: The mishna on 20a, side by side: what each form of words costs as a valuation and as an assessment, with the Gemara’s additions.

messages.text: With regard to one who valuates in order to donate half the valuation of a vessel,

notes.dh: ת"ר המעריך חצי ערך כלי ר"מ אומר נותן דמיו
notes.he: ה"ג ברוב הספרים ולא נראה דא"כ מאי קאמר בסמוך פלגיה לאו אורחיה לאינדובי ואמאי אין דרך להתנדב חצי שוייה של כלי לכך נראה לר"י דה"ג המעריך ערך חצי כלי והשתא ניחא דאמר פלגיה לאו אורחיה לאינדובי דחצי כלי אין שוה כלום ומשום הכי קאמר פלגיה לאו אורחיה לאינדובי:
notes.en: The Sages taught: one who valuates half the valuation of a vessel, Rabbi Meir says he gives its assessment: so most books read, and it does not seem right, for if so, what does it mean just below, “half, it is not the usual way to donate”? Why should it not be usual to donate half the worth of a vessel? So the Ri holds that the reading is “one who valuates the valuation of half a vessel.” Now it works out that he says “half, it is not the usual way to donate,” because half a vessel is worth nothing; that is why he says “half, it is not the usual way to donate.”

messages.text: He gives half the assessment of the vessel.
He has not said anything.

notes.he: כשהעריך חצי כלי אבל העריך כלי שלם נותן את דמיו:
notes.en: And the Rabbis say he has not said anything: when he valuated half a vessel; but if he valuated a whole vessel, he gives its assessment.

messages.text: Rava became sick, and Abaye and other Sages came to visit him.

Granted that Rabbi Meir holds that a person does not utter a statement for naught, and therefore there is no difference whether one vowed to donate the entire valuation of a vessel, and there is no difference whether one vowed to donate half its valuation; in either case he must have intended to donate the assessment, as there is no valuation with regard to vessels.
messages.lead: As they were sitting and talking, they said:

notes.he: ואשמועינן בחציו וכ"ש בכולו דאע"ג דלאו אורחא לאינדובי חצי דמי כלי אפ"ה יהיב וכ"ש כולו:
notes.en: No difference whether all of it, no difference whether half of it: and it teaches us half of it, and all the more so all of it; for although it is not the usual way to donate half the value of a vessel, even so he gives, and all the more so all of it.

messages.text: But with regard to the Rabbis in the baraita, what do they hold? If they maintain that a person utters a statement for naught, then even if one vowed to donate the entire valuation of a vessel, he should be exempt and the Rabbis should disagree with regard to that case. And if the Rabbis maintain that a person does not utter a statement for naught, then even one who vowed to donate half the valuation of a vessel should be obligated to give half of the assessment.

notes.he: אפי' אמר ערך כלי זה עלי ליפטר:
notes.en: Even all of it as well: even if he said, “The valuation of this vessel is incumbent upon me,” he should be exempt.

messages.text: The Rabbis here in the baraita hold in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Meir, but they also hold in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon.
messages.lead: Rava and Abaye said to the Sages in response:
messages.quote: But with regard to the Rabbis in the baraita, what do they hold?

messages.text: They hold in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Meir, who says that a person does not utter a statement for naught, and therefore one who vows to donate the valuation of a vessel must give its assessment.

notes.he: ומש"ה לא פליג בכולו:
notes.en: They hold like Rabbi Meir: and that is why they do not disagree about all of it.

messages.text: And they also hold in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon with regard to one who consecrated an item for a purpose for which it was unsuited, e.g., if one sought to bring a barley meal offering even though meal offerings may be brought only from wheat (see Menaḥot 103a). Rabbi Shimon says he is exempt from any obligation, as this person did not donate in the manner typical of donors.

notes.he: ר"ש פוטר האומר הרי עלי מנחה מן השעורין בפ"ב דמנחות (דף קג.):
notes.en: Rabbi Shimon exempts one who says, “I take upon myself a meal offering of barley,” in Menaḥot (103a) [the printed Rashi says “in the second chapter” of Menaḥot].

messages.text: So too, with regard to one who vows to donate the valuation of a vessel, it is the typical manner for one to donate an entire vessel, and therefore one who does so is obligated to donate the assessment of the vessel. But it is not the typical manner for one to donate half a vessel, and therefore one who vows in this manner has not said anything and is exempt.

notes.he: [סברי לה כר"מ דאמר אין אדם מוציא דבריו לבטלה היכא דהתנדב כדרך המתנדבים דהעריך כולו פלגיה לאו אורחא לאינדובי הלכך לא אמר כלום דסבר לה כר' שמעון]:
notes.en: [They hold like Rabbi Meir, who says a person does not utter his words for naught, where he donated in the manner of donors, when he valuated all of it. Half, it is not the usual way to donate; therefore he has not said anything, since they hold like Rabbi Shimon.]

messages.text: § What is the specific case to which the mishna is referring? It must be referring to a case where he stood in judgment, and the court obligated him to donate his valuation before he died. The court’s ruling is considered like a financial obligation written in a document, and therefore the heirs of the one who vowed are required to pay his valuation.
messages.quote: It is incumbent upon me to donate the valuation of so-and-so, and both the one who vowed and the object of the vow die

notes.he: כלומר מתני' דקתני יתנו היורשין היכי מיתוקמא בע"כ כשעמד בדין קודם מותו כדאוקמא לרישא ואמאי הדר קתני לה:
notes.en: What is it? Where he stood in judgment: that is, how can the mishna that teaches “the heirs give” be explained? Necessarily where he stood in judgment before his death, as we explained the first clause; so why does it teach it again?

notes.he: האומר ערכו של פלוני עלי [ומת הנודר והנידר. אמאי יתנו היורשין בשעמד בדין המעריך קודם שמת]:
notes.en: What is it: one who says, “The valuation of so-and-so is incumbent upon me,” [and both the one who vowed and the object of the vow died: why should the heirs give? Where the one who valuated stood in judgment before he died.]

messages.text: If so, this clause in the mishna is identical to that previous clause in the mishna, which states that if one said: It is incumbent upon me to donate my valuation, and he dies, his heirs must give his valuation to the Temple treasury. Since it was explained that the earlier clause is also dealing with a case where he stood in judgment, for what purpose was this halakha repeated in the mishna?

notes.he: בשמעתין דלעיל אמר ערכי עלי ומת יתנו היורשין ואוקימנא כשעמד בדין:
notes.en: That is the same: in the passage above, one said “My valuation is incumbent upon me” and died, the heirs give, and we explained it as where he stood in judgment.

messages.text: It was necessary to repeat this halakha in order to teach the latter clause of the mishna: With regard to one who says it is incumbent upon him to donate the assessment of so-and-so, and the one who vowed dies, his heirs must give his assessment to the Temple treasury.
messages.quote: the assessment of so-and-so, and the one who vowed dies, his heirs must give

messages.text: This is necessary lest you say: Although the one who took the vow stood in judgment before he died and the court obligated him, since the object of his vow was not assessed before he died, the property of the one who vowed is not liened to the debt, and consequently the heirs are not obligated to pay.

notes.he: אע"ג דעמד בדין נודר קודם מותו הואיל ולא אמדו נידר בחיי נודר לא אשתעבדו נכסי דיתמי:
notes.en: Lest you say: although the one who vowed stood in judgment before his death, since the object of the vow was not assessed in the lifetime of the one who vowed, the property of the orphans [his heirs] is not liened.

messages.text: Therefore, the mishna teaches us that the property of the one who took the vow was liened, since he stood in judgment while he was still alive, and the assessment of the object of the vow is considered to be a mere disclosure of the matter, which can be performed after the death of the one who vowed.

notes.he: לגלות מהו חייב והואיל ונידר קיים אמדינן ליה:
notes.en: It is a mere disclosure of the matter: to reveal how much he owes; and since the object of the vow is alive, we assess him.

notes.he: להקדש:
notes.en: The property was liened: to the Temple.

notes.he: ואומדנא כיון דלאו בנודר תליא אלא בנידר מאי דרמי עליה דנודר לשלומי חייבוהו ב"ד ויורשין חייבין ואומדנא גלוי מלתא בעלמא הוא דכל אדם יכול לאומדו אפילו אינו ב"ד ומה שיאמר שום אדם שהיה שוה יתנו הנודר אבל (באומד דתלוי עליו) [באומר דמי עלי] ומת כיון דהוא גופיה בעי אומדנא ולא אמדוהו יורשין פטורין:
notes.en: And the assessment: since it depends not on the one who vowed but on the object of the vow, whatever lay upon the one who vowed to pay, the court obligated him, and the heirs are obligated; and the assessment is a mere disclosure of the matter, for anyone can assess him, even someone who is not a court, and whatever any person says he was worth, [the heirs of] the one who vowed shall give. But [with one who says “My assessment is incumbent upon me”] and dies, since he himself needs to be assessed and they did not assess him, the heirs are exempt.

messages.text: Mishna

In the case of one who says: This bull is consecrated as a burnt offering, or: This house is consecrated as an offering, and the bull died or the house collapsed, he is exempt from paying his commitment.

notes.he: לבדק הבית:
notes.en: Mishna. And this house is an offering: for Temple maintenance.

notes.he: קודם שהחזיק בו גזבר:
notes.en: And the house collapsed: before the Temple treasurer took possession of it.

notes.he: לדמיו:
notes.en: And this house is an offering: for its value.

notes.he: מלשלם שהרי אמר זה ולא קבל עליו אחריותו:
notes.en: Exempt: from paying, since he said “this” and did not accept responsibility for it.

messages.text: But in the case of one who says: It is incumbent upon me to give this bull as a burnt offering, or: It is incumbent upon me to give this house as an offering, if the bull died or the house collapsed, he is obligated to pay its value.

notes.he: קיבל עליו אחריותו וחייב לשלם:
notes.en: But if he said “upon me”: he accepted responsibility for it, and is obligated to pay.

messages.text: Gemara
The Sages taught in the mishna only that one who said: It is incumbent upon me to give the monetary value of this bull as a burnt offering, is obligated to pay its value if it dies.
messages.quote: It is incumbent upon me to give this bull as a burnt offering

notes.he: דכי אמר עלי חייב לשלם אלא דאמר דמי עלי דאם אבד השור הדמים לא אבדו דהא לא אמר דמים הללו ולא היו בעין:
notes.en: Gemara. They taught only — that when he said “upon me” he must pay — where he said “the monetary value is incumbent upon me”: for if the bull is lost, the value is not lost, since he did not say “this money,” and it was not in existence.

notes.he: דחייב באחריותו:
notes.en: They taught only: that he bears responsibility.

notes.dh: אלא דאמר דמי שור זה עלי
notes.he: כלומר שאם (נגנב) [יוגנב] אתחייב בדמיו:
notes.en: But where he said “The monetary value of this bull is incumbent upon me”: that is, if it is stolen, I am obligated for its value.

messages.text: But if he said: It is incumbent upon me to give this bull as a burnt offering, since he said: This, thereby referring specifically to that animal, and then the bull died, he does not bear financial responsibility for its loss. And as for his statement: It is incumbent upon me, he did not intend to accept financial responsibility for the loss of the bull. Rather, he meant to say: It is incumbent upon me to bring this bull as an offering to the Temple.

notes.he: לטרוח עד שיתקרב:
notes.en: Upon me to bring it: to take the trouble until it is offered.

notes.he: [עלי להביאו קאמר אם יהיה]:
notes.en: [He meant: it is upon me to bring it, if it exists.]

notes.he: אמר ר' חייא בר רב ל"ש אלא דאמר דמי שור זה עלי עולה אבל אמר שור זה עלי עולה כיון דאמר זה ומת אינו חייב באחריותו עלי להביאו קאמר - כלומר לטרוח עד שיתקרב וא"ת א"כ רישא דמתני' דקתני שור זה עולה מת השור פטור מלשלם [לאשמועינן] אפילו אמר עלי (נראה כן) הדין [כן] דפטור מלשלם כדמסיק ר' חייא בר רב ואור"י דכולה מתני' בין רישא בין סיפא מיירי דאמר דמי וה"פ דמתני' דמי שור זה עולה דמי בית זה קרבן מת השור נפל הבית פטור מלשלם כיון דלא אמר עלי אבל אמר דמי שור זה עלי עולה דמי בית זה עלי קרבן מת השור ונפל הבית חייב לשלם והכי איתא בפ"ק דר"ה (דף ו. ושם) איזהו נדר ואיזהו נדבה נדר דאמר עלי נדבה דאמר הרי זו מה בין נדר לנדבה נדר מת או נגנב חייב באחריותו נדבה מת או נגנב אינו חייב באחריותו והא דתניא במתני' שור זה נראה דרבותא אשמועינן דאע"ג דאמר זה כיון דאמר עלי חייב באחריותו ואר"י דלכאורה משמע דכי אמר דמי שור זה עלי עולה גוף השור הוא חולין ואין בו קדושה דדמי לאומר דמי שור של פלוני עלי דגוף השור הוא חולין דאין אדם מקדיש שור חבירו ולא דמי למקדיש זכר לדמיו דאמר בתמורה (דף יט: ושם) דקדוש קדושת הגוף דמגו דנחתא ביה קדושת דמים נחתא ביה קדושת הגוף דהתם מיירי כדאמר יקדש שור זה לדמיו וה"נ איתא בסמוך בשמעתין דכי אמר יקדש השור לדמיו דגוף השור קדוש:
notes.en: In brief: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Rav explains “upon me” in “this bull is upon me” as “upon me to bring it,” that is, to take the trouble until it is offered. Tosafot ask: if so, what does the first clause of the mishna, “This bull is a burnt offering … exempt from paying,” teach us, when even with “upon me” he is exempt, as Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Rav concludes? The Ri says the whole mishna, first clause and latter clause, speaks of one who said “the monetary value”: “The value of this bull is a burnt offering,” “the value of this house is an offering,” and the bull died or the house fell, he is exempt, since he did not say “upon me”; but “the value of this bull is upon me as a burnt offering,” “the value of this house is upon me as an offering,” he must pay. So it is in Rosh HaShana (6a): a vow is where he said “upon me,” a gift offering is where he said “this is”; with a vow, if it died or was stolen he bears responsibility, with a gift offering he does not. The mishna’s “this bull” teaches a novelty: although he said “this,” since he said “upon me” he bears responsibility. The Ri adds that at first sight, one who says “the value of this bull is upon me as a burnt offering” leaves the bull itself non-sacred, like one who says “the value of so-and-so’s bull is upon me,” where the bull stays non-sacred because a person cannot consecrate another’s ox. It is not like one who consecrates a male animal for its value, which Temurah (19b) says receives inherent sanctity (once sanctity of value comes upon it, inherent sanctity comes upon it too), since there he said “let this bull be consecrated for its value”; and so below in our passage, when he says “let the bull be consecrated for its value,” the bull itself is sacred. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

messages.text: With regard to one who says: This bull is consecrated as a burnt offering, the bull is consecrated property and one who benefits from it is liable for misuse of consecrated property. If the bull dies or is stolen, he does not bear financial responsibility for its loss.
messages.lead: The Gemara raises an objection from a baraita:

messages.text: If one says: It is incumbent upon me to give this bull as a burnt offering, the bull is consecrated property, and one who benefits from it is liable for misuse of consecrated property. If the bull dies or is stolen, he bears financial responsibility for its loss, despite the fact that he did not vow to give the monetary value of the bull.

notes.he: מיתיבי שור זה עולה כו' שור זה עלי עולה השור הקדש ומועלין בו מת או נגנב (אינו) חייב באחריותו - אלמא לא אמרינן עלי להביאו קאמר וקשיא לר' חייא ומשני מי אלימא ממתניתין דאוקימנא דקאמר דמי הכא נמי דקאמר דמי וקשה לפי מה דפי' דגופו חולין ובהא ברייתא קתני דשור קדוש ולפי מה דפירש"י הכא ניחא וזה לשונו הכא נמי דקאמר דמי וכדאוקימנא לקמן דקאמר יקדש השור לדמיו והדמים עלי עולה הלכך השור קדוש דהא אמר יקדש השור ואם מת חייב באחריותו דהא עלי אמר והכא לא אמר עלי להביאם קאמר דכיון דלא הוו דמים קמיה ולא אמר דמים הללו עלי עולה ליכא למימר כדאמר לעיל דהתם כיון דאמר זה למפטר נפשיה מאחריות קאתי ועלי אטורח הבאה קאי אבל הכא דלא הוו הדמים קמיה ולא אמר הללו ודאי עלי אאחריות קאי והא דקאמר זה ה"ק שור זה יהיה הקדש עד שאמכרנו ואביא דמיו. עכ"ל רש"י:
notes.en: In brief: The baraita says “This bull is upon me as a burnt offering: the bull is consecrated, one is liable for misuse of it, and if it died or was stolen he bears responsibility.” So we do not say “he meant: upon me to bring it,” which is difficult for Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Rav; and the Gemara answers that, as with the mishna, the baraita speaks of one who said “the monetary value.” Tosafot ask: according to the explanation [of the Ri, in the previous Tosafot] that in such a case the bull itself is non-sacred, how can the baraita say the bull is consecrated? According to Rashi’s explanation here it works out, and Tosafot quote Rashi’s note on “Here too, he says ‘monetary value’” in full: that the case is “Let this bull be consecrated for its value, and its value is upon me as a burnt offering,” so the bull is sacred and he bears responsibility; and that “upon me” here refers to responsibility, not to the trouble of bringing it, since the money was not before him and he did not say “this money.” Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: [כיון דאמר עלי] אע"ג דלא אמר דמי:
notes.en: If it died or was stolen he bears responsibility for it: [since he said “upon me”], even though he did not say “monetary value.”

messages.text: Is the baraita stronger than the mishna, with regard to which we established that it is referring to a case where he says: The monetary value of the bull? Here too, in the case of the baraita, he says: It is incumbent upon me to give the monetary value of this bull as a burnt offering.
messages.quote: he bears financial responsibility for its loss

notes.he: וכדאוקימנא לקמן דאמר יקדש שור זה לדמיו והדמים עלי עולה הלכך השור קדוש דהאמר יקדש השור ואם מת חייב באחריותו דהאמר עלי והכא ליכא למימר כדאמר לעיל דהתם כיון דאמר זה למפטר נפשיה מאחריות אתי ועלי אטורח הבאה קאי אבל הכא דלא הוו דמים קמיה ולא אמר הללו ודאי עלי אאחריות קאי והאי דקאמר זה הכי קאמר שור זה יהא קדוש עד שאמכרנו ואביא דמיו:
notes.en: Here too, he says “monetary value”: as we explain below, that he said “Let this bull be consecrated for its value, and the value is upon me as a burnt offering.” So the bull is sacred, since he said “let the bull be consecrated,” and if it died he bears responsibility, since he said “upon me.” And here one cannot say as was said above, that since he said “this” he meant to exempt himself from responsibility and “upon me” refers to the trouble of bringing it. Here, where the money was not before him and he did not say “this [money],” “upon me” certainly refers to responsibility; and when he said “this,” he meant: let this bull be sacred until I sell it and bring its value.

messages.text: But from the fact that the latter clause of the baraita is referring to a case where he says: Monetary value of, it may be inferred that the first clause of the baraita is referring to a case where he does not say monetary value. As it teaches in the latter clause of the baraita:

notes.dh: והא מדסיפא דקאמר דמי רישא דלא קאמר דמי דקתני סיפא כו'
notes.he: וה"ה דהוה מצי למיפרך בהדיא מסיפא אמתני' לפי מה דפי' ר' חייא בר רב דקתני בסיפא דמי זה עלי עולה השור חולין ואין מועלין בו מת או נגנב אינו חייב באחריותו ובמתני' תנן דחייב לשלם אלא לפי מה שהתחיל לאקשויי מרישא סיים קושייתו עלה ולפי התירוץ ניחא הכל [אבל] קשיא על הא דאיתא בפ' בתרא דחולין (דף קלט. ושם) המקדיש מנה לבדק הבית ונגנב או שאבד רבי יוחנן אמר חייב באחריותו עד שיבא ליד הגזבר ורשב"ל אמר כל היכא דאיתיה בי גזא דרחמנא איתיה דכתיב לה' הארץ ומלואה וקדשי בדק הבית אע"ג דאמר עלי לא מחייב והא תנן האומר שור זה עולה בית זה קרבן מת השור ונפל הבית פטור לשלם שור זה עלי עולה בית זה עלי קרבן מת השור ונפל הבית חייב לשלם ומאי קפריך הא דרשב"ל מיירי כשהפריש המנה שהקדיש ומש"ה קאמר דכל היכא דאיתיה בי גזא דרחמנא איתיה ואינו חייב לשלם וההיא דמתני' בשלא הפריש כלום ומש"ה קתני דחייב לשלם דהא אוקימנא דהשור גופיה חולין ונראה דלית ליה להאי סוגיא דהתם הא דר' חייא בר רב דמוקי למתני' בדמי לכך נראה לר"י דהכא במתני' דגוף השור קדוש כמו מקדיש זכר לדמיו דקדוש קדושת הגוף ולא דמי לאומר שור חבירו עליו דאין גופו קדוש דהתם אין אדם יכול להקדיש ממון חבירו ומיהו כל מה דמצי למתפיס ביה הוא מתפיס אבל הכא שהשור שלו כי אמר דמי שור זה עלי עולה גוף השור קדוש והשתא ניחא דפריך בפרק בתרא דחולין (ג"ז שם) מהאי מתני' ארשב"ל דכיון דגוף השור קדוש הוי כמו הפרישו ודמי למקדיש מנה לבדק הבית וניחא נמי בשמעתין דפריך מברייתא דשור זה עלי עולה וכו' ומשני דקאמר והשור הוי הקדש כדקתני וה"נ מתני' הוי גוף השור הקדש ומיהו תימה קצת אמאי צריך לאוקמי כדמסיק רישא דאמר יקדש שור לדמיו בלא"ה נמי כיון דאמר דמי שור זה עלי עולה הוי גוף השור הקדש וצ"ל דה"פ רישא כי הוה אמר יקדש שור לדמיו והוי שור הקדש ועי"ל דהא דאר"ח בר רב לא שנו אלא דאמר דמי שור זה עלי עולה פי' דאמר יקדש שור לדמיו ודמיו עולה והוי גוף השור קדוש ובהכי ניחא כולה שמעתא וניחא נמי האי דפ"ב דחולין (ג"ז שם) ופריך ממתני' דהכא אר' שמעון בן לקיש דכיון דגוף השור קדוש הוי כאילו הפריש ודמי למקדיש מנה לבדק הבית:
notes.en: In brief: The Gemara could have objected straight from the latter clause of the baraita to the mishna as Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Rav explains it, since that clause says “the value of this [bull] is upon me as a burnt offering: the bull is non-sacred … if it died or was stolen he does not bear responsibility,” while the mishna says he must pay; but having begun its objection from the first clause, it finished it there, and the answer settles everything. A difficulty: in Ḥullin (139a), on one who consecrated a maneh for Temple maintenance and it was stolen or lost, Rabbi Yoḥanan says he bears responsibility until it reaches the treasurer, and Reish Lakish says that wherever it is, it is in the treasury of the Merciful One (“The earth is the Lord’s, and its fullness”), so even with “upon me” he is not obligated; and the Gemara there objects to Reish Lakish from our mishna, “This bull is upon me as a burnt offering … he must pay.” What is the objection? Reish Lakish speaks of one who set the maneh aside, and our mishna of one who set nothing aside, since we explained the bull itself as non-sacred. It seems that passage does not accept Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Rav’s explanation that the mishna speaks of “monetary value.” So the Ri holds that in our mishna the bull itself is sacred, like one who consecrates a male animal for its value, which receives inherent sanctity. It is unlike one who takes his fellow’s bull upon himself, which does not become sacred because a person cannot consecrate another’s property (though whatever he can apply sanctity to, he does); here the bull is his own, so when he says “the value of this bull is upon me as a burnt offering,” the bull itself is sacred. Now the objection in Ḥullin works, since a sacred bull is as though he set it aside, like one who consecrated a maneh; and our passage works too, objecting from the baraita and answering that the bull is consecrated as it teaches, and so too in the mishna. A small difficulty remains: why must the first clause be explained as “let the bull be consecrated for its value,” when saying “the value of this bull is upon me” already makes the bull sacred? One must say the first clause is read as though he said “let the bull be consecrated for its value,” and the bull is sacred. Or else Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Rav’s “only where he said ‘the value of this bull is upon me’” itself means he said “let the bull be consecrated for its value, and its value as a burnt offering,” and the bull is sacred; with that the whole passage works, and so does the objection in Ḥullin from our mishna to Reish Lakish. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

messages.text: With regard to one who said: It is incumbent upon me to give the monetary value of this bull as a burnt offering, the bull is non-sacred property and one who benefits from it is not liable for misuse of consecrated property. If the bull dies or is stolen, he does not bear financial responsibility for its loss. But if he sold the bull and received money for the sale, he does bear financial responsibility for that money, since he accepted financial responsibility for the monetary value of the bull in his vow.

notes.he: דלא הקדיש אלא מעות דמי השור לכשימכר:
notes.en: The bull is non-sacred: for he consecrated only the coins of the bull’s value, once it is sold.

notes.he: שהרי לא נמכר ונמצא שלא הקדיש כלום:
notes.en: He does not bear responsibility for it: since it was not sold, it turns out he consecrated nothing.

notes.he: אם נמכר השור וקדשו הדמים ואבדו חייב באחריותו:
notes.en: But he does bear responsibility for its value: if the bull was sold and the money became sacred and was lost, he bears responsibility for it.

notes.he: שלא הקדישו אלא דמיו] (אינו חייב באחריותו דדמי השור קאמר וכיון דמת אין דמים למתים כדאמרינן במתני' דמי עלי ומת לא יתנו היורשין):
notes.en: [The bull is non-sacred: since he consecrated only its value.] (He does not bear responsibility, since he spoke of the value of the bull, and once it died there is no monetary value for the dead, as we say in the mishna: “My assessment is incumbent upon me,” and he died, the heirs do not give.)

messages.text: The first clause and the latter clause of the baraita are both referring to one who says: Monetary value of, in his vow. The difference between them is that the first clause is dealing with one who says: Let the bull be consecrated for its monetary value, and therefore the bull is consecrated and he bears financial responsibility for its value.

notes.he: והלכך חייב באחריותו שהרי חל קדושת דמים על השור והוא קיבל עליו אחריות דמיו והאי עלי אחריות הוי הואיל ואדמים קאי ודמים לא הוו קמיה דלימא הללו:
notes.en: The first clause is where he said “Let the bull be consecrated for its value”: so he bears responsibility, since sanctity of value took effect on the bull and he accepted responsibility for its value; and this “upon me” means responsibility, since it refers to the value, and the value was not before him that he could say “this.”

notes.dh: רישא דאמר יקדש השור עלי לדמיו
notes.he: דכיון דאמר יקדש השור קדוש השור ומועלין בו וכיון דאמר לדמיו היינו דאמר מת או נגנב חייב באחריותו:
notes.en: The first clause is where he said “Let the bull be consecrated, upon me, for its value”: since he said “let the bull be consecrated,” the bull is sacred and one is liable for misuse of it; and since he said “for its value,” that is why it says that if it died or was stolen he bears responsibility.

messages.text: But the latter clause is referring to one who says: When this bull shall be sold, the money received from the sale shall be consecrated for use as a burnt offering.

notes.he: הלכך אינו חייב באחריותו דכיון דמת השור ולא בא לכלל דמים נמצא שלא הקדיש כלום:
notes.en: The latter clause is where he said “When its value comes, let it be consecrated”: so he does not bear responsibility, for since the bull died and never came to be money, it turns out he consecrated nothing.

notes.he: [וסיפא דאמר לכשיבואו דמיו יקדשו כשימכר דכיון דלא אמר יקדש השור לפיכך לא קדש ואין חייב באחריותו]:
notes.en: [And the latter clause is where he said “When its value comes, let it be consecrated,” when it is sold; since he did not say “let the bull be consecrated,” it is not consecrated, and he does not bear responsibility.]

messages.text: Can this possibly be the case of the latter clause of the baraita? But a person cannot consecrate an entity that has not yet come into the world, and therefore one cannot consecrate the money he will receive in the future from the sale of the bull.
messages.quote: When this bull shall be sold, the money received from the sale shall be consecrated

notes.dh: והא אין אדם מקדיש דבר שלא בא לעולם
notes.he: והיכי קדשי הני דמים לכשיבואו:
notes.en: But a person cannot consecrate something that has not come into the world: so how do these coins become sacred when they come?

messages.text: In accordance with whose opinion is this baraita? It is taught in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Meir, who says: A person can consecrate an entity that has not yet come into the world.

notes.he: דתניא הרי את מקודשת לי לאחר שאתגייר לאחר שתתגיירי כו' ר"מ אומר מקודשת:
notes.en: It is Rabbi Meir: as it is taught: “You are betrothed to me after I convert,” “after you convert,” etc.; Rabbi Meir says she is betrothed.

notes.he: [דאמר אדם מקדיש דבר שלא בא לעולם] במס' קדושין:
notes.en: It is Rabbi Meir: [who says a person can consecrate something that has not come into the world], in tractate Kiddushin.

messages.alt: or Rami bar Ḥama, to Rav Ḥisda
messages.text: In accordance with whose opinion is this baraita? Is it in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Meir, who says that a person can consecrate an entity that has not yet come into the world?
messages.lead: Some say a slightly different version of this discussion, that Rav Pappa said to Abaye, and some say Rami bar Ḥama said to Rav Ḥisda:

messages.text: Rather, in accordance with who else’s opinion could this baraita be? Certainly it is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Meir.

messages.caption: The baraita’s three bulls as the Gemara reads them: what was said, whether the bull itself becomes consecrated, and who bears the loss if it dies or is stolen.

messages.text: And some teach this discussion with regard to this baraita:

notes.he: להא דרב יהודה ואביי ורמי בר חמא:
notes.en: And some teach it: this statement of Rav Yehuda, and of Abaye and of Rami bar Ḥama.

messages.text: In the case of one who rents a house to another and the house became ritually impure with leprosy, even though a priest confirmed the house as impure, condemning it to be dismantled, as long as the house is still standing its owner may say to the renter: That which is yours is before you, and the owner is not required to compensate the renter.

notes.he: שאמר טמא הוא ועומד לנתץ כל זמן שלא נתצו אומר לו משכיר לשוכר הרי שלך לפניך ולא אשכיר לך בית אחר שהרי בית שהשכרתי לך קיים:
notes.en: Even though a priest confirmed it: saying it is impure and stands to be dismantled. As long as he has not dismantled it, the landlord says to the renter, “That which is yours is before you,” and I will not rent you another house, since the house I rented you is standing.

notes.dh: אע"פ שחלטו כהן אומר לו הרי שלך לפניך
notes.he: אור"י דמהכא משמע דבית מנוגע המוחלט מותר בהנאה ומש"ה אומר לו הרי שלך לפניך דדמי להא דתנן פרק האומנין (ב"מ עח. ושם) שכר חמור והבריקה או שנעשית אנגריא אומר לו הרי שלך לפניך דאי אמרינן דבית הנחלט אסור בהנאה אם כן הוי כי מתה או נשברה דתנן התם חייב להעמיד לו חמור אחר וקשה למורי מהא דאמר בתורת כהנים גבי בגדים צרעת ממארת תן לה מארה שלא יהנה ממנו משמע דאסור בהנאה וכן משמע בפרק מצות חליצה (יבמות קג:) א"ר פפא משמיה דרבא [סנדל] המוסגר לא תחלוץ ואם חלצה חליצתה כשרה סנדל המוחלט לא תחלוץ ואם חלצה חליצתה פסולה ופרש"י שם דסנדל המוסגר לא תחלוץ בו לכתחלה משום גזירה דסנדל המוחלט מיהו אם חלצה חליצתה כשרה משום דמצות לאו ליהנות ניתנו אלמא משמע סנדל המוחלט אסור בהנאה וצ"ל דאין הכי נמי דהוא אסור בהנאה והא דאמר הכא דאומר לו הרי שלך לפניך היינו כגון דא"ל בית זה וכיון דהוא בעין אינו חייב להעמיד לו בית אחר מיהו הוא הפסיד שכרו והוי כמו מתה או נשברה דאמר התם חייב להעמיד לו חמור אחר ופרש"י שם או יפסיד שכרו:
notes.en: In brief: The Ri says this shows that a confirmed leprous house is permitted for benefit, which is why the landlord can say “that which is yours is before you,” as in the mishna in Bava Metzia, chapter HaUmanin (78a): one who hired a donkey and it went blind or was seized for royal service, [the owner] says “that which is yours is before you.” Were a confirmed house forbidden for benefit, it would be like a donkey that died or broke a leg, where the mishna there says he must provide another donkey. But my teacher found this difficult: Torat Kohanim says of garments, “a malignant [mam’eret] leprosy,” give it a curse [me’era], that one may not benefit from it, which implies it is forbidden for benefit. So too in Yevamot, chapter Mitzvat Ḥalitza (103b), Rav Pappa says in the name of Rava: with a quarantined sandal she should not perform ḥalitza, but if she did, her ḥalitza is valid; with a confirmed sandal she should not, and if she did, her ḥalitza is invalid. Rashi there explains that with a quarantined sandal she should not do it at the outset, by decree because of a confirmed one, yet it is valid because mitzvot were not given for benefit; so a confirmed sandal is forbidden for benefit. One must therefore say that it is indeed forbidden for benefit, and “that which is yours is before you” is where he said “this house”: since it is still standing he need not provide another house, but he loses his rent, as with a donkey that died or broke a leg, where it says there he must provide another donkey, and Rashi there adds, or lose his fee. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: ברשות השוכר אע"פ שחלטו הכהן ואסור בהנאה:
notes.en: And it became afflicted: in the renter’s possession; even though the priest confirmed it and it is forbidden for benefit.

notes.he: שאין יכול לומר הרי שלך לפניך מה שמכרת:
notes.en: [A note in the printed text: it seems it should read] the landlord says to the renter, “That which is yours is before you,” what you rented. [Even a landlord to a renter; for he cannot say “That which is yours is before you” about what he sold.]

messages.text: Nevertheless, in accordance with the halakha of a house afflicted with leprosy, once the priest has dismantled the house the owner is obligated to provide a new house for the renter.

notes.he: כהן חייב משכיר להעמיד בית אחר לשוכר דמשום מזליה דמשכיר הוא שנחשד על הגזל או על צרות העין:
notes.en: He dismantled it: the priest did; the landlord must provide the renter with another house, for this came about through the landlord’s fortune, since he is suspected of theft or of stinginess.

notes.he: כהן:
notes.en: He dismantled it: the priest did.

messages.text: Continues on 21a: the baraita goes on to a rented house that is consecrated, and there the Gemara again asks how one can consecrate money that has not yet come into the world.
